title: Why Am I Downgrading This Hall of Fame Stock?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc downgrades Mastercard from BUY to HOLD after the stock soared from $470 in June to $661 - up 15.8% year to date plus dividends, outperforming the S&P 500 with lower risk. He has owned it since around 2020 and ranked it a buying opportunity several times this year, but at $661 it sits well above his $573 intrinsic value, so there is no margin of safety for new buyers. The business remains a Hall of Fame name: analysts now expect 16.7% annual EPS growth (up from ~13% in mid-2025), revenue growth near double digits, a 59% operating margin (above 55% for most of the last decade), and a 46% operating-cash-flow-to-sales ratio. The Visa duopoly keeps competition limited, which supports industry-wide profitability. He stresses he is not selling any of his own shares and expects the stock could earn an upgrade again before long if the price stays flat while performance improves. Verdict: HOLD at ~$661, DCF fair value $573.
